claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a conventional coarse-grained bulk microstructure.
High-energy shot peening or laser surface treatment can form the proposed graded nanohierarchical layer in situ on CoCrFeNi.
The engineered surface layer will contain nano-coupled grains, finely and uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates, and gradients in grain size and composition.
A nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can provide adaptive friction-interface protection from room temperature to 800 °C.
At room temperature, coexisting deformation pathways in nano-coupled grains release or distribute frictional stress in stages.
Room-temperature stress distribution through multiple deformation modes minimizes plastic damage and friction.
At elevated temperature, the fine grains and nanoprecipitates promote rapid tribochemical oxidation and formation of a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
The high-temperature glaze layer is lubricious.
The dense nanocrystalline glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear at 800 °C.
The nanostructured CoCrFeNi surface will have a lower wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The nanostructured CoCrFeNi surface will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The treatment may reduce friction coefficient and wear rate by one to two orders of magnitude relative to untreated CoCrFeNi.
The proposed performance domain is sliding in ambient air from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under normal loads of 5–20 N.
A reciprocating sliding test at 5 N with continuous friction monitoring and wear-volume-based wear-rate measurement is experimentally feasible.
Treated and untreated CoCrFeNi samples can be compared under identical load, speed, atmosphere, and temperature conditions to test the intervention.

The hypothesis is falsified if the treated samples fail to show statistically significant, approximately order-of-magnitude reductions in both friction coefficient and wear rate across the full temperature range, or if the adaptive layer is not sustained.
